text:
Creekside Park improvement project to begin with demolition on Sept. 8
The Creekside Park Improvement Project in Brookfield is scheduled to start with the demolition of the existing park hardscape on Tuesday, Sept. 8. Half of the $1.2 million project will be funded by a federal Open Space Lands Acquisition and Development grant of $600,000, administered through the Illinois Department of Natural Resources.
The Village Board of Trustees is expected to award a construction contract for planned improvements at its meeting on Sept. 14. Demolition work is not included in that contract and will instead be carried out by Brookfield Public Works staff beginning Sept. 8.
During demolition, one dumpster will be placed along the west side of Grove Avenue just south of Burlington Avenue. No Parking signs are set to be installed in that area this week, and construction notices will be hand-delivered to residents living on Burlington Avenue east of Forest Avenue and Grove Avenue between Burlington and Southview.
Brookfield Public Works’ scope includes removal of the park’s fence, playground equipment and foundations, all existing concrete curb, stone council ring and bench, metal path edging, as well as one tree. Construction for new playground amenities is expected to begin later in September.
Planned features include a multi-colored blue and green poured-in-place playground safety surface; play structures such as an ages 5-12 apparatus; market discovery station; freestanding play panel; two-bay swing set; Comet II spinner; a new shelter; ornamental fencing with swing gate; unisex restroom building; baggo court; ADA-accessible game tables; trash receptacles and benches; drinking fountain; interpretive sign; plus new plantings featuring native species like dogwood, butterfly weed, yarrow, coneflower, black-eyed Susan, aster, salvia, iris and little blue stem.
Brookfield operates as a municipal local government focused on civic administration services including public works projects like this one while providing residents with utility billing support, code enforcement oversight for property maintenance issues, permitting processes for construction or renovation projects within village limits—as well as public safety services through its police department, according to the official website.
